beats.role_note: COLD OPEN -- required fellow intro line + AI-voice disclosure; ask lands answered
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Boopesh M., and this video is about what got in the way for the Humanitarians AI fellows this week, November eighth to the fourteenth. A quick note: this is an AI voice reading my script. Every number comes from the git history and the fellows' own frictional logs, counted by a small script.

props.command: What got in the way for the Humanitarians AI fellows from Nov 8 to Nov 14? Read their frictional logs.
output: 32 frictional logs from 13 fellows · 31 describe obstacles
top theme: layout & picture checks, in 19 logs
17 logs: the problem was found by someone looking

beats.role_note: BLUF -- hesitant writer corrects the misconception
beats.narration_text: Here's the week in one line. You might guess the hardest part was installing the tools. But the most common obstacle was checking the result.

props.text: The hardest part was installing the tools.

beats.role_note: 31 logs with obstacles sorted into six plain themes (rough keyword sort), bar chart
beats.narration_text: Thirty-two frictional logs were added this week, by thirteen fellows, and thirty-one describe obstacles. I sorted them by keywords into six plain themes. It's my rough sort, and one log can land in several. Layout and picture checks led, in nineteen logs from eight fellows: things running off the edge, overlapping, or too small to read. Then facts and data, in eleven. Length and time, ten. Tools and setup, ten. Timing and pacing, eight. And the AI voice saying a word wrong, five.

beats.role_note: five short paraphrased examples, obstacle -> fix, one per theme, folder names only
beats.narration_text: A few examples, in my words. A chart passed the frame checks, but showed the opposite of the narration. A working title didn't survive the data, so the title changed. A script ran four minutes twenty-two for a four-minute slot, and was trimmed five times without cutting a number. A checking script took over forty minutes; now it streams frames, in eighty-seven seconds. And words on screen appeared late, until each reveal was timed to the voice.

beats.role_note: what fixed them: 17 of 31 logs found a problem by looking; the takeaway
beats.narration_text: So what fixed them? Most often, someone looked. In seventeen of the thirty-one logs, a problem was found by watching the cut, viewing the frames, or re-reading the words. A passing check tells you the frame fits. Only looking tells you it's right.

beats.role_note: ONE comparison with last week (same script, recounted today)
beats.narration_text: One comparison with last week, recounted today by the same script. Merged pull requests: nineteen, down from twenty-seven. New work folders: fifty-three, from seventy-five. Fellows with new folders: seventeen, from nineteen. And frictional logs: thirty-two, from ninety-five.

beats.role_note: Boopesh's own two videos last week; delivered for review; his own obstacle: access
beats.narration_text: And my part. Last week I made two videos. What the Fellows Taught runs two fifteen. The Backtest Mirage, on AI in finance, runs two twenty-four. Each has a Short, all four are 4K, delivered for review. My own obstacle is access: my fork attempt failed, so my pull request is still pending, and my folder isn't on main, or in these counts.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF -- prompt read aloud and explained
beats.narration_text: Your turn. With your own project open, paste this into Claude. Read my frictional log from this week. Sort what got in the way into three plain themes, and for each one, suggest one check I can do by eye before my next build. A good answer quotes the line each theme comes from.

props.command: Read my frictional log from this week. Sort what got in the way into three plain themes, and for each one, suggest one check I can do by eye before my next build. Quote the lines.

beats.narration_text: What got in the way. With Boopesh M., for Humanitarians AI. Thanks for watching.
